*Comprehensive market data examining the costs, timelines, and challenges of traditional app development hiring in 2027*


The global developer population[reached 47.2 million](https://www.slashdata.co/blog/global-developer-population-trends-2025-how-many-developers-are-there) in 2025, yet[72% of employers](https://www.manpowergroup.com/cs/news-releases/news/global-talent-shortage-reaches-turning-point-as-ai-skills-claim-top-spot) reported difficulty filling roles across industries in 2026. Although these figures measure different populations, they highlight important considerations for founders planning to hire technical talent.


AI-assisted development offers another path. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) enable non-technical founders to build working web and mobile applications through supported AI assistants, reducing the need for traditional hiring on suitable projects. The statistics below examine development costs, hiring timelines, talent shortages, and AI adoption trends heading into 2027.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Floot offers an alternative to traditional hiring:** Founders can[build full-stack apps](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) through supported AI assistants, with Floot managing the backend infrastructure. The platform is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) .
- **Developer hiring costs remain substantial:** Typical app development projects cost[$10,000 to $49,000](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) , while the median annual wage for US software developers reached[$135,980](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) in May 2025.
- **Hiring timelines create additional challenges:** Average time to hire[reached 41 days](https://app.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) in 2024, representing a 24% increase since 2021 across the roles measured.
- **The technology talent gap persists:**[65% of technology hiring managers](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-technology-roles-are-in-highest-demand) reported finding skilled professionals harder than the previous year.
- **AI adoption is changing development workflows:**[83% of surveyed technologists](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data) use AI tools at work, while a[controlled coding experiment](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/the-impact-of-ai-on-developer-productivity-evidence-from-github-copilot/) found 55.8% faster completion of one specific task with GitHub Copilot.


## **Understanding the Costs of Hiring App Developers**


The financial commitment required to bring an app from concept to launch often surprises first-time founders. Between hourly rates, project fees, and ongoing maintenance, costs can escalate quickly.


### **1. Most app development projects cost $10,000 to $49,000**


The typical mobile app development project requires[$10,000 to $49,000](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) to fully complete and launch, according to Clutch data cited by Adapty. This range applies to commonly reported projects, with enterprise-grade solutions potentially commanding significantly more.


### **2. Average developer hourly rates range from $25 to $49**


According to app development pricing data, typical developer hourly rates range from[$25 to $49](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) . Actual rates vary depending on geographic location, developer experience, and project complexity. Additional requirements such as custom features, third-party integrations, and ongoing maintenance can increase overall development costs.


### **3. US software developers earned a median of $135,980 annually in 2025**


The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the median annual wage for software developers was[$135,980 in May 2025](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) . This figure covers software developers broadly rather than mobile app specialists alone. Employer costs may also include benefits, equipment, and management overhead.


### **4. iOS developers charge $50 to $75+ per hour**


According to app development pricing data, iOS developers skilled in Swift, Objective-C, and Xcode typically charge[$50 to $75 or more](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) per hour. Rates may increase for experienced developers handling complex features, advanced integrations, or specialized app requirements. Geographic location and project scope also influence overall hiring costs.


### **5. Android developers charge $45 to $90+ per hour**


Android app development rates generally range from[$45 to $90 or more](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) per hour for developers working with Java, Android SDK, and related technologies. Pricing varies based on developer experience, geographic location, and application complexity. Projects involving custom functionality, third-party integrations, or advanced technical requirements may cost more.


### **6. North American development rates range from $80 to $150 per hour**


According to software development outsourcing estimates, development rates in North America typically range from[$80 to $150 per hour](https://www.freshcodeit.com/blog/software-development-outsourcing-statistics-and-trends) . These figures reflect outsourced software development costs rather than fixed rates for all developers. Actual pricing depends on technical specialization, project complexity, team structure, and required development services.


## **Key Statistics on App Development Timelines**


Hiring app developers involves multiple stages, from sourcing candidates to interviews and final selection. These statistics highlight average hiring timelines, increasing recruitment complexity, and delays that can affect project schedules and time-to-market.


### **7. Average time to hire increased 24% since 2021**


Hiring timelines expanded, with[average time to hire](https://app.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) growing from 33 days in 2021 to 41 days in 2024. Gem's recruiting benchmark reported this as a 24% increase across the hiring processes studied. This eight-day increase highlights longer recruitment cycles and growing hiring complexity across the roles studied.


### **8. Engineering roles averaged 62 days to fill in an older benchmark**


An earlier[Workable hiring benchmark](https://resources.workable.com/tutorial/faq-time-to-fill-hire) reported a global average time to fill of 62 days for engineering roles. It also cited a separate SHRM benchmark of 42 days across roles. These are historical time-to-fill figures, not current 2027 hiring estimates.


### **9. Hiring teams conducted 42% more interviews per hire**


The interview process intensified, with teams conducting[42% more interviews](https://app.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) per hire in 2024 than in 2021. Gem's benchmark reported an increase from 14 to 20 interviews per successful hire across the hiring process. This rise highlights growing recruitment complexity and the additional effort required to evaluate candidates.


### **10. Candidates were 3x less likely to be hired in Gem's 2025 benchmark**


Gem's 2025 recruiting benchmarks found that candidates were[3x less likely](https://app.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) to be hired than three years earlier. This reflected lower candidate progression rates through the recruiting funnel rather than a measured increase in app development time.


## **The Demand and Supply of Skilled App Developers**


The global developer population continues growing, yet the gap between available talent and employer needs persists. Understanding these dynamics helps explain why alternative development approaches are gaining traction.


### **11. Global developer population reached 47.2 million in 2025**


The worldwide developer population[grew to 47.2 million](https://www.slashdata.co/blog/global-developer-population-trends-2025-how-many-developers-are-there) in early 2025, according to SlashData's global developer population estimates. This growth reflects sustained interest in software development careers, although the total includes professional and non-professional developers.


### **12. Professional developer population reached 36.5 million in 2025**


The global professional developer population[reached 36.5 million](https://www.slashdata.co/blog/global-developer-population-trends-2025-how-many-developers-are-there) in early 2025, up from 21.8 million in early 2022. This growth reflects an expanding professional workforce, although specialized hiring challenges remain.


### **13. 72% of employers reported difficulty filling roles in 2026**


[72% of employers](https://www.manpowergroup.com/cs/news-releases/news/global-talent-shortage-reaches-turning-point-as-ai-skills-claim-top-spot) globally reported difficulty filling positions across industries in ManpowerGroup's 2026 survey of 39,000 employers across 41 countries. This figure reflects overall hiring challenges rather than IT-specific vacancies.


### **14. 65% of technology hiring managers find skilled candidates harder to locate**


[65% of technology hiring](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-technology-roles-are-in-highest-demand) managers said finding skilled professionals was more challenging than a year earlier, according to Robert Half's 2026 research. Skills shortages affected initiatives involving AI integration, security, and software development.


### **15. 51% of surveyed CTOs cite specialist IT skills gaps**


In a 2025 study of 500 chief technology officers,[51% identified specialist](https://www.akkodis.com/en/newsroom/news/reality-of-ai-strategy-in-entreprise-today) IT skills as the leading capability gap. The Akkodis findings highlight broader technical talent challenges organizations face when adopting AI, but the figure does not specifically measure AI and machine learning skills shortages.


## **Popular Technologies and Frameworks for App Development**


The technology landscape shapes hiring requirements and project complexity. Understanding current frameworks helps founders make informed decisions about their development approach.


### **16. 14.2% of surveyed developers use Android Studio**


In the 2026 Stack Overflow Developer Survey,[14.2% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/technology/data/dev-ide) reported using Android Studio regularly during the previous year. This measures development-tool usage rather than the total number of Android-only developers worldwide.


### **17. 10.0% of surveyed developers use Xcode**


In the 2026 Stack Overflow Developer Survey,[10.0% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/technology/data/dev-ide) reported using Xcode regularly during the previous year. This provides a development-tool usage benchmark without implying an exact global count of iOS-only developers.


### **18. React Native developers charge $24 to $45 per hour**


Developers working with React Native typically charge[$24 to $45](https://www.upwork.com/hire/react-native-developers/cost/) per hour on Upwork, while Flutter developers generally charge[$18 to $39](https://www.upwork.com/hire/flutter-freelancers/) per hour. These marketplace ranges reflect historical contracts and listed rates, with actual costs depending on experience, location, and project scope.


## **Leveraging AI and Low-Code Platforms to Reduce Hiring Needs**


The rise of AI-assisted development tools is changing how applications get built. These statistics illustrate growing adoption of AI in development workflows, although adoption does not necessarily mean organizations are replacing developers.


### **19. 83% of surveyed technologists use AI tools at work**


Approximately[83% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data) to Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey reported using at least one AI tool at work. This widespread adoption highlights AI's growing role in software development workflows.


### **20. 73% of AI coding-assistant users use them daily**


Among respondents using AI coding assistants,[73% reported daily use](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data) in Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey. This indicates frequent usage among coding-assistant users rather than all developers.


### **21. 97% of HackerRank-surveyed developers use AI assistants**


HackerRank reported a[97% AI assistant adoption rate](https://www.hackerrank.com/reports/developer-skills-report-2025) among developers in its 2025 surveyed audience, indicating widespread use within that group. Additionally, 61% reported using two or more AI tools at work, demonstrating how multiple tools are incorporated into development workflows.


### **22. GitHub Copilot users completed one coding task 55.8% faster**


In a controlled experiment, participants using GitHub Copilot completed a JavaScript HTTP-server task[55.8% faster](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/the-impact-of-ai-on-developer-productivity-evidence-from-github-copilot/) than those without it. This task-specific result does not establish equivalent savings across complete development projects.


### **23. GitHub reported Copilot completing 46% of code in enabled files**


GitHub's early research found that[46% of code](https://github.blog/news-insights/research/the-economic-impact-of-the-ai-powered-developer-lifecycle-and-lessons-from-github-copilot/) was completed by Copilot in files where it was enabled. Separately, an Accenture study found that developers accepted[around 30% of Copilot suggestions](https://github.blog/news-insights/research/research-quantifying-github-copilots-impact-in-the-enterprise-with-accenture/) . These figures represent different research populations and should not be generalized to all developers.


### **24. 26.2% of surveyed technologists use AI agents or automated workflows**


In Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey,[26.2% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) reported using AI agents or automated workflows at work. This measures professional AI-tool adoption rather than the percentage of apps containing generative AI features.


## **Statistics on Outsourcing vs. In-House App Development**


Organizations weighing build-versus-buy decisions need reliable data on outsourcing effectiveness. The numbers reveal why organizations consider alternatives to in-house hiring.


### **25. 76% of surveyed executives outsourced IT functions in 2022**


Deloitte's 2022 Global Outsourcing Survey found that[76% of surveyed](https://www.deloitte.com/middle-east/en/our-thinking/mepov-magazine/securing-the-future/the-power-of-third-party-assurance-reporting-in-todays-world.html) global executives used third-party models to deliver IT services. This historical result demonstrates the prevalence of IT outsourcing at the time, but it should not be presented as a measured 2027 outsourcing rate.


### **26. Eastern European developers charge $30 to $60 per hour**


Freshcode estimates Eastern European rates at[$30 to $60 per hour](https://www.freshcodeit.com/blog/software-development-outsourcing-statistics-and-trends) and Indian developer rates at $15 to $50 per hour. These regional pricing differences highlight potential cost advantages when outsourcing app development. Actual rates depend on developer experience, technical specialization, project complexity, and location.


### **27. 57% of surveyed organizations cite talent access as an outsourcing driver**


An IT sourcing study by PA Consulting and Whitelane found that[57% of surveyed organizations](https://www.paconsulting.com/insights/three-ways-to-triumph-in-the-it-talent-tussle) cited access to talent and resources as a reason for outsourcing. The result identifies an important motivation alongside others, rather than the single primary reason for outsourcing.


## **Mobile App Market Growth and Technology Hiring Trends**


The mobile app market continues its expansion, creating sustained demand for development resources while highlighting the scale of opportunity for founders.


### **28. Mobile app development market valued at $302.1 billion in 2025**


The global mobile app development market[reached $302.1 billion](https://straitsresearch.com/report/mobile-app-development-market) in 2025 and is projected to reach $844.50 billion by 2034, representing a 12.1% CAGR during the 2026–2034 forecast period.


### **29. Market projections reach $988.5 billion by 2035**


Market Research Future separately projects the mobile app development market[reaching $988.5 billion](https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/mobile-app-development-market-1752) by 2035, with a CAGR of 23.8% from a substantially lower 2025 baseline of $116.87 billion. Its estimates differ from those of Straits Research and should not be directly compared.


### **30. 61% of tech leaders planned headcount increases for H1 2026**


Robert Half's 2026 research reported that[61% of technology leaders](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-technology-roles-are-in-highest-demand) planned to increase permanent headcount earlier in the year. By the second half of 2026, that share had risen to 78%. These figures describe hiring intentions rather than confirmed hiring outcomes.


## **Build and Publish Full-Stack Apps with Floot Instead of Hiring Developers First**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that allows founders to create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected assistant handles development while Floot supplies managed infrastructure, including PostgreSQL databases, authentication, storage, payments, email, and hosting.


Floot helps founders:


- Build working web applications without first hiring a traditional developer.
- Use an existing AI subscription for development through the[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , subject to client permissions.
- Start with the Free plan and upgrade as building and hosting requirements grow.
- Create iOS and Android builds without installing Xcode or Android Studio locally.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) . Pro costs $25/month and Power costs $100/month, with different daily building-action limits, hosting allowances, and mobile-build limits. Hosting overages and optional AI features may incur separate charges.[Mobile publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) requires the relevant developer accounts and store approval. Users own their code and data, while full project ZIP export is a paid feature.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the average cost to hire an app developer?**


Clutch data cited by Adapty places common[app development rates](https://adapty.io/blog/hire-mobile-app-developers/) between $25 and $49 per hour, though US-based developers may charge substantially more depending on specialization. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a median annual software developer wage of[$135,980](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) in May 2025. Commonly reported complete app projects cost between $10,000 and $49,000, depending on scope.


### **How long does it typically take to hire an app developer?**


Developer hiring timelines vary by role and recruiting process. Gem's 2025 recruiting benchmark found that average time to[hire increased from 33 days](https://app.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) in 2021 to 41 days in 2024 across the roles studied. This measures recruiting time, not the time required to develop an application. Founders can explore[AI-assisted MVP development](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-mvp-development) while evaluating their hiring needs.


### **Can AI tools like Floot replace the need for hiring traditional app developers?**


For many MVPs and straightforward applications, AI-assisted tools can reduce the need to hire developers. A[controlled coding study](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/the-impact-of-ai-on-developer-productivity-evidence-from-github-copilot/) found 55.8% faster completion of one task. With[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , supported assistants can build and publish working applications, although complex projects may still require developer expertise.


### **What are the benefits of using Floot for app development?**


Floot provides managed application infrastructure including PostgreSQL databases, user authentication, file storage, and hosting. Users can build through supported AI assistants using their existing subscriptions, without separate Floot AI build-credit charges for standard connector actions. The[Floot pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) are free to start, with paid options for increased building allowances, hosting, and additional capabilities. Floot also supports[mobile app publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) for iOS and Android, subject to developer-account requirements.


### **What are some common challenges in hiring skilled app developers?**


[72% of employers](https://www.manpowergroup.com/cs/news-releases/news/global-talent-shortage-reaches-turning-point-as-ai-skills-claim-top-spot) globally reported difficulty filling roles across industries in 2026, while[65% of technology hiring managers](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-technology-roles-are-in-highest-demand) said finding skilled professionals had become harder. Gem's 2025 benchmark found that average time to hire increased 24% between 2021 and 2024. These challenges can add time and uncertainty to app development plans, particularly for founders who need specialized technical skills.
